meta.title: Operation of Ultrasonic Bath in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To facilitate sonication-assisted extraction of bioactive compounds from plant materials, improve solubility of crude extracts, and degas solvents prior to HPLC or TLC analysis.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for enhanced extraction of phytochemicals using acoustic cavitation, degassing of mobile phases, and cleaning of botanical extraction equipment.
procedure: Fill the ultrasonic bath tank with tap water or distilled water to the minimum fill line — use distilled water for prolonged extraction work.
Set the operating temperature if required (room temperature to 40°C for most extraction work).
Switch on and allow the bath to reach temperature equilibration (5–10 minutes).
For solvent degassing: place the solvent bottle (cap loosened) or flask of solvent directly in the bath and run for 10–15 minutes.

For sonication-assisted extraction: place the plant material + solvent in a sealed conical flask or tube; submerge this vessel in the water bath — do not add plant material directly to the bath water.
Set the timer for the required sonication time: typically 20–45 minutes for plant extraction.
Switch on the transducers — confirm operation by the characteristic hissing sound and surface rippling.
Do not submerge open vessels containing volatile organic solvents directly — always seal or use indirect method.
Monitor temperature — prolonged sonication heats the bath; cool with ice if temperature-sensitive extraction.
After completion, switch off transducers and remove samples.
Filter extracts immediately using Whatman No. 1 filter paper or Buchner funnel.
Drain and rinse the bath with clean water after use; clean with dilute detergent weekly.
Record material, solvent system, sonication time, temperature, and yield in the laboratory logbook.
precautions: Do not operate without water in the tank — dry running permanently damages the transducers.
Do not place bare hands in the bath during operation — cavitation causes tissue injury.
Do not use flammable solvents directly in the bath — always seal in a closed vessel and use water as the coupling medium.
Keep the liquid level above the minimum fill line throughout operation.
Do not use at maximum temperature for prolonged periods — overheating degrades the transducer bond.
Inspect the tank for pitting, corrosion, or cracks monthly — replace if degraded.
Replace tank water regularly — contaminated water reduces acoustic coupling efficiency.
